findings.title: intcomma leaves finite negative numbers ungrouped
findings.cause: After coercion, negative inputs still start with '-' but the grouping regex only matches strings that begin with digits, so the loop returns the original negative string unchanged.
findings.impact: Negative balances, counts, and deltas are formatted less readably than positive values and violate the function's advertised integer/float grouping behavior.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:164 formats orig from the numeric value
src/humanize/number.py:171-174 applies r'^(\d+)(\d{3})', which cannot match '-1234567'
tests/test_number.py:41-83 covers positive intcomma cases and non-finite negatives but no finite negative values
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add cases such as assert humanize.intcomma(-1234567) == '-1,234,567' and assert humanize.intcomma(-1234567.89) == '-1,234,567.89'.

findings.title: fractional loses or duplicates the sign for negative fractions
findings.cause: The code truncates the whole part with int(number), computes a signed Fraction from the remainder, then uses abs(numerator) only for values with no whole part and leaves the signed numerator in mixed fractions.
findings.impact: Negative fractional values are misrepresented: values between -1 and 0 become positive, while negative mixed values render with a double negative component.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:370-382 computes whole_number and numerator without preserving one clear sign for the result
tests/test_number.py:166-189 covers positive fractional inputs and non-finite negatives but no finite negative fractions
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add cases such as assert humanize.fractional(-0.3) == '-3/10' and assert humanize.fractional(-1.3) == '-1 3/10'.

findings.title: clamp marks exact floor and ceil values as out of range
findings.cause: The comparisons use <= for floor and >= for ceil even though the docstring says only values smaller than floor or larger than ceil should receive the clamp token.
findings.impact: Boundary values displayed in dashboards or reports get misleading '<' or '>' prefixes even when they are exactly within the allowed range.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:464-475 documents strict smaller/larger behavior and includes clamp(0.99, ceil=0.99) -> '99%'
tests/test_number.py:223-240 covers below-floor and above-ceil cases but not equality
repro output: clamp(0.99, format='{:.0%}', ceil=0.99) -> '>99%'; clamp(0.01, floor=0.01) -> '<0.01'
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add equality cases for floor and ceil, e.g. assert humanize.clamp(0.99, format='{:.0%}', ceil=0.99) == '99%' and assert humanize.clamp(0.01, floor=0.01) == '0.01'.

findings.title: ordinal applies suffix rules to negative remainders
findings.cause: Suffix selection uses value % 100 and value % 10 directly; Python modulo makes -1 select the 9 suffix slot and -2 select the 8 suffix slot.
findings.impact: Finite negative ordinals render with incorrect suffixes such as '-1th' and '-2th', which is visible for signed rankings or offsets.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:105-107 selects suffixes from modulo results on the signed value
tests/test_number.py:14-38 covers positive ordinal values and non-finite negatives but no finite negative ordinals
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add finite negative ordinal cases such as assert humanize.ordinal(-1) == '-1st' and assert humanize.ordinal(-2) == '-2nd'.

findings.title: naturalsize has no non-finite float guard
findings.cause: The function converts input with float(value) but never checks math.isfinite before comparing and taking log(abs_bytes). NaN reaches int(min(log(...))) and raises, while infinity is formatted with the largest suffix.
findings.impact: Telemetry or filesystem-size inputs containing NaN or infinity either crash formatting or produce a misleading value such as 'inf QB', unlike the number APIs that normalize non-finite values to 'NaN', '+Inf', or '-Inf'.
evidence: src/humanize/filesize.py:89-101 converts to float, branches on abs_bytes, then logs without a finite check
src/humanize/number.py:21-31 defines the shared non-finite display convention used by number helpers
tests/test_filesize.py:12-96 has no NaN or infinity naturalsize cases
repro output: naturalsize(math.nan) -> ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer; naturalsize(math.inf) -> 'inf QB'
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add cases for math.nan, math.inf, and -math.inf, either expecting the same non-finite strings as number helpers or an explicitly documented exception.
